title: Scale offset nudge log
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal scratchpad for the weird precision/NaN regression seen on nightly int8 runs when enabling per-token caching + small batch sizes. This is a living note — trying to capture commands, observed failures, hypotheses, and quick repro steps so we (I) don't forget details between experiments.

Summary of symptom:
- Intermittent NaNs in activations during generation, usually after ~120–400 tokens depending on seed and batch shape.
- Only reproducible when: int8 weights used, KV cache enabled (streaming), batch_size <= 2, and sequence length distribution skewed (long prefix + short streamed tokens).
- If model switched to bf16 weights (no int8 quant), NaNs disappear. If int8 + disable KV cache, NaNs largely disappear.
- Happens on both A100 and T4; more frequent on T4.

Timeline (session notes):
2025-02-14 09:15 — baseline run
- command: python reproduce_streaming.py --model-model=rw-v1 --quant=int8 --kv-cache true --batch 1 --seed 42
- result: NaN at step 187, stack trace points to matmul in attention kernel (cuda kernel name: matmul_attn_fp32_accum)
- quick dump: activation[14] = inf, activation[15] = nan

2025-02-15 11:30 — kernel swap experiment
- toggled env: TORCH_USE_CUDA_KERNELS=0 (fallback to cuBLAS path)
- result: still NaN but shifted token index (260). Kernel names changed in trace. Suggests not a single kernel bug.

2025-02-16 15:00 — scale/clamp mitigation test
- patched runtime to clamp attention scores: max_score = min(max_score, 50.0) before softmax.
- result: NaNs gone for ~8 runs but reappeared eventually at later tokens.
- suggests extremely large intermediate logits sometimes produced.

Commands tried (repro):
- python -u tests/quant_repro.py --model rw-small --quant int8 --cache on --batch 1 --seq 512 --seed 7
- CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 python -u tests/quant_repro.py ... (useful to get exact failing kernel)
- TF32 off/on variations: export CUDA_TF32_OVERRIDE=0/1
- switch backend: export QUANT_BACKEND=fbgemm | qnnpack | custom

Err snippets (copied raw):
- RuntimeError: CUDA error: device-side assert triggered at /.../matmul_kernel.cu:423
- Tensor values: att_scores mean=4.2e+03 std=1.1e+03 max=1.2e+06 min=-9.8e+05
- Guard log: quant_dequant_scale=0.0001839, zero_point=128

Observed patterns:
- Scale factors fluctuate a lot across layers; layer-wise per-channel scales sometimes underflow to subnormals (1e-38) after calibration pass when using small calibration set.
- Softmax stability: extremely large logits cause overflow in exp even when using float32 accumulation in some fused kernels.
- Residual-add mismatch: when residual path kept in bf16 and main path in int8->accum fp32, casting order seems to matter (residual + dequant(main)) sometimes produces infs while the reverse order doesn't.

Hypotheses:
1) Calibration dataset too small / skewed -> extremely small scales for some channels; dequantization multiplies by huge numbers for activations leading to overflow in attention matmuls.
2) Mixed-precision accumulation differences across kernels cause slightly different rounding that, in long chains (streaming + KV cache), accumulate to extreme logits.
3) KV cache quantization: caching quantized keys/values and then dequantizing at different timestamps introduces drift (scale mismatch between cache write-time and read-time) — if scale stored per-chunk rather than per-timestep, drift can compound.
4) Tiny denorm handling on certain GPUs (T4) causing slow underflow then abrupt jump when another op scales it.

Experiments to run (ordered):
A) Deterministic small repro: generate 4 different seeds, fixed input prompt, log per-layer max/min/scale after calibration (save to JSON). Goal: reproduce consistent seed that fails.
- command: python tools/save_scales.py --model rw-small --quant int8 --calib-size 512 --out=calib-scales.json

B) Disable per-channel quant and use per-tensor scales: does it reduce instability? If yes -> calibration or per-channel tail behavior to blame.

C) Try online recalibration on cache read: when reading keys/values, recompute/adjust scales based on current activation stats (cheap approximate) to detect drift.

D) Add conservative clamp on logits and softmax input as temporary mitigation; measure quality impact on eval prompts (perplexity + sample quality).

E) Force all residual adds to do (dequant(main) -> cast to bf16 -> add residual) vs (cast residual -> add dequant) to see which ordering avoids infs.

Quick reproducer (mini):
- minimal script: tests/min_repro.py (attached idea)

# tests/min_repro.py (pseudo)
# ---------
# model = load_model('rw-tiny', quant='int8', cache=True)
# prompt = 'A' * 120
# for i in range(400):
#   out = model.step(prompt if i==0 else '\n')
#   if torch.isfinite(out).all() == False:
#       print('NaN at step', i)
#       dump(layer_stats)
#       break

Quick patches attempted:
- clamp before softmax as mentioned.
- during cache write, store fp16 versions of keys/values as a fallback (double memory) — reduced NaNs but memory spike unacceptable.
- small change in quantization: force min_scale = 1e-5 during calibration; helped for several runs.

Open questions / notes to self:
- Is the calibration pass deterministic between runs on different hardware? I saw scale vectors differ more than expected between A100 and T4 for same seed. Might be nondeterminism in reduction ops.
- How are scales stored with KV cache across restarts? If a different worker reads cached chunks with different global scaling policy, mismatch can occur.
- Check PR #789 for recent quant scale packing change — could be regression (linked above).

Next steps (immediate):
- Run A and B experiments overnight with full debug logging (per-layer min/max/scale) and link artifacts to Jira AIINF-1023.
- If reproducible seed found, create a minimal CI test that runs quant streaming for 100 steps and asserts no non-finite values.
- Talk to @Ravi about adding a tiny safety quant floor in calibration codepath.

Notes to future self:
- Keep the temp scale floor conservative (1e-6) — avoid hurting dynamic range for layers that need very small scales.
- Consider per-layer calibration sets (some layers need different stats).

Attachments/commands to copy later:
- CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 python -u tests/quant_repro.py --model rw-small --quant int8 --cache on --batch 1 --seq 512 --seed 7 &> qrun.seed7.log
- python tools/extract_layer_stats.py qrun.seed7.log --out qrun.seed7.stats.json

References / bookmarks:
- internal thread: slack#eng-inference "int8 streaming NaN" (Feb 12–16)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/789
- Jira: AIINF-1023

End of scratchpad.

(Will iterate — keep this file as the canonical running diary for the problem.)
